thread.title: Stock Market Dives; How IBD's Rules Dodged Apple's Pain

author: EdJenner
title: Stock Market Dives; How IBD's Rules Dodged Apple's Pain
text:
U.S. stock indexes Monday headed toward a third straight session of losses, casting doubt on the bullish case for the stock market.
X
The Nasdaq staggered 2.5% lower, while the S&P 500 declined 1.5%. Blue chips in the 30-component Dow bowed 1.6%. Small caps fell 1.7% in the Russell 2000’s gauge.
Volume in the stock market quieted on both major exchanges.
Although three daily losses in a row is creating doubt about the stock market’s bullish signal Wednesday, the weekly charts don’t look bad. The Nasdaq, S&P 500 and Dow charts show two weekly gains in a row — not a profile that would normally encourage the bears. Trouble In The Stock Market
Monday’s stock market gave the bears plenty to like as some big-name players tumbled.
On Monday, Apple ( AAPL ) and Boeing ( BA ) weighed on the Dow. Apple carved off about 5%. Boeing sliced off about 3%.
Apple notched its lowest mark in 15 weeks. The stock has now unwound all the gains from its Aug. 1 breakout. In early October, the gain from the 194.30 breakout reached 20%. The 20% profit level is a place to take profits. IBD research shows that most stocks will begin to consolidate after a 20% to 25% gain from a breakout. That’s exactly what happened in Apple’s case.
On Monday, Lumentum ( LITE ) said an unnamed customer cut orders. The unnamed customer is believed to be Apple. Lumentum collapsed 31%. Handling Apple
IBD-style investors sell on the chart action alone, not the news. The disciplined investor either would’ve sold Apple when the stock reached the 20% profit level in October or sold when the profit threatened to cycle into a loss.
Meanwhile, Boeing has its own set of problems. A low-volume, July breakout triggered the 8% sell rule in August. A breakout in September advanced 8% and then retreated to trigger the 8% sell rule in late October.
Large-cap Boeing is currently struggling to find support at its 50-day line. Small Cap Rises
Among small caps, restaurant chain Wingstop ( WING ) advanced 3% in the first 20 minutes of trade. But the gain faded to 0.7%. Wingstop retook its 50-day line Thursday and is holding above that key area.
Wingstop gapped up to a breakout Aug 3. Because the gap-up opened above the ideal buy point, the realistic entry was the 56.34 price at the open. The stock sprinted 34% above the entry before pulling back recently.
Wingstop is now 21% above the breakout price.
Among IBD’s 197 industry groups, the day’s top 12 performers included food, soap and utilities. The day’s losers included the chip and biomed groups.
